company: Revolution Private Credit Income Trust (Responsible Entity: Equity Trustees Limited)
title: Listed Investment Trusts Trading Policy

tiers.name: EQT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, key management personnel and all employees of EQTHL and/or any of its wholly or majority owned companies including the Responsible Entity, and contractors and consultants who may come into possession of Inside Information. Subject to prior written clearance from the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary via the Trading Request Procedure.

tiers.name: LIT Partners
tiers.description: Those engaged or contracted with the Responsible Entity in managing and/or administering a LIT. May trade under their own trading policy/procedures agreed with the Responsible Entity (rather than the EQT Trading Request Procedure), but must disclose LIT Person transactions to the Company Secretary within 7 days.

tiers.name: LIT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and consultants of a LIT Partner or any other related account as defined by the LIT Partner's trading policy. Subject to the LIT Partner's own trading policy, which must at least match this Policy's Black-out Periods and insider trading prohibition.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse, partner or child of an EQT Person, or any other person whom the EQT Person may be expected to control or have significant influence over, including other immediate family members, business partners, companies or other entities or trusts. Must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Responsible Entity may specify 'any other period' as a Black-out Period (clause defining Black-out Period, item v); the policy does not state whether such additional periods are confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. Unit includes an option over an unissued unit or a right to subscribe, and Trade means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units; a bespoke OTC put/call over Units would be caught as trading an economic interest and requires prior written clearance, subject to Black-out Periods and no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units, including electing to vary a dividend reinvestment plan ("DRP") participation.

rules.detail: Hedging or other financial arrangements limiting the economic risk of holding Units are expressly addressed and permitted only with prior written clearance under the Trading Request Procedure; no distinction is drawn by vesting state since Units held by these persons are not typically subject to a vesting schedule under this policy.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure transfers an economic interest in Units and so is a Trade requiring prior written clearance, and if it involves granting security it is also caught by clause 6(iii).
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named and is not obviously caught by the Trade definition (which covers buy, sell or transfer of an economic interest already or about to be acquired, not a short sale).
Securities lending of Units is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing Units would transfer economic exposure to Units and so falls within the Trade definition, requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly named and permitted only with prior written clearance under the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons , LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security over Units is expressly covered by the broad wording 'any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units', permitted only with prior clearance.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons , LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Any arrangement (not limited to margin lending) where security is granted over Units is expressly covered and permitted only with prior written clearance; no outright ban.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons , LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Short-term or speculative on-market trading within three months of acquisition is prohibited unless prior written clearance has been approved.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not engage in short-term or speculative trading in a LIT's Units, i.e. trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance ... A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.

exemption_authority: The Responsible Entity's Chair may determine 'any other exceptional circumstances' warranting a trade despite a Black-out Period (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair where the trading person is the Responsible Entity's Chair); the Company Secretary consults the Chair on such proposals. Irrespective of any clearance or exemption, a person possessing Inside Information is prohibited from trading in all circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.topic: encumbrance and margin lending permitted with clearance
bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on Units is not banned outright; it is structurally available subject to prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, unlike policies with an absolute secured-financing prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar (put, call and any encumbrance) would need to be priced and executed within 5 business days of clearance being granted, which is tight for negotiating bank documentation and may require re-clearance if timing slips.

bespoke_clauses.topic: clearance refusal is unreasoned and final
bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretary has unfettered, unreviewable discretion to refuse or withdraw clearance for the collar or loan, and any refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant, so approval cannot be assumed or appealed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance to trade is not an endorsement of the proposed trade and that the person doing the trading is individually responsible for their investment decisions and compliance with insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Obtaining clearance does not shift insider trading risk to the Responsible Entity; the executive and the bank must independently confirm no Inside Information exists at signing and settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the event that any of the Black-out Periods specified in clauses i, ii, or iii above apply concurrently, the Black-out Period specified in clause iii will apply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: PDS/prospectus-related Black-out Periods (up to 28 days before lodgement) can override and extend the standard half-year/year-end windows, adding scheduling uncertainty for collar entry or unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Responsible Entity undertakes a buy-back of units in a LIT, the EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An executive involved in a unit buy-back faces an additional, deal-specific trading freeze beyond the standard calendar windows.

summary: A funded collar over vested Units appears structurally available under this policy: hedging arrangements that limit the economic risk of holding Units, and margin lending or any other arrangement granting security over Units, are both expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary, rather than banned. Clearance is discretionary, can be refused or withdrawn without reasons (a final and binding, confidential decision), and once granted is valid for only five business days, so the put, call and security must be documented and executed promptly within that window and outside the applicable Black-out Periods (half-year/year-end NTA release windows, PDS/prospectus windows, general meeting windows, and any buy-back-specific window). The executive must not hold Inside Information at execution regardless of clearance, and clearance is expressly not an endorsement of the trade. The three-month short-term/speculative trading restriction should also be considered for tenor and any early unwind. Overall, subject to case-by-case clearance and tight timing, the funded collar is achievable.
